title: The Illusion of Randomness: How LLMs Fail to Emulate Stochastic Decision-Making in Rock-Paper-Scissors Games?

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4.1 Configurations (temperature 1, top-p 1, repetition penalties disabled); max_tokens assumed

task.subset_rule: 100 independent single-turn games, a new session (fresh conversation) per call
task.approximation: the paper's 'GPT-4-turbo' alias is resolved to the 2024-04-09 snapshot by rule (EMNLP Findings 2025, no version string)

items.source: Sec. 4.2 prompt box (the prompt is the entire input; footnote 2 spells out RPS and {R, P, S})

prompt.user_template: You are playing the Rock-Paper-Scissors game. You should first reason about the Nash equilibrium of this game, and then choose one action from {Rock, Paper, Scissors} based on your reasoning. Please choose an exact action.
prompt.source_location: Sec. 4.2 prompt box (below Table 1) with footnote 2 expansions ('RPS' -> 'Rock-Paper-Scissors', '{R,P,S}' -> Rock, Paper, Scissors)
prompt.verbatim: full (abbreviations expanded exactly as footnote 2 states; note the literal braces around the action set are part of the prompt, not a placeholder)

output.parse: final chosen action: last occurrence of Rock / Paper / Scissors in the reply after the reasoning (prefer patterns 'choose <X>', 'action: <X>', '**<X>**'); replies naming none or several actions without a final pick are invalid
output.postprocess: lowercase; invalid replies dropped and the empirical distribution renormalized over {rock, paper, scissors} (Eq. 3)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: TVD = 0.5 x sum_a |1/3 - p_hat(a)| over the three actions, p_hat from the 100 games (Eq. 4); mean over seeds

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare 2026-09-07: est_usd_prepare counts <=400 output tokens per free-text call (runner out_guess); est_usd_dryrun_max_tokens counts the full max_tokens

notes: The per-action shares (Figure 2) are a finer check.
